title: wb sdd amend: add a file to an audited plan without redoing it
desc:
When implementation needs a file the plan missed, the only way forward today is to hand-edit sdd.json, copy the zones from wb repo zones, and rerun the audit. The loop costs more than the file, and a hand edit is also where a zones block or a why goes stale.

amend is the narrow door: it adds a path to a plan that already passed, and it leaves a record that the plan grew mid-flight.

ACCEPTANCE:
- wb sdd amend <KEY> <path>... --why "<reason>" appends {path, why} to files, recomputes zones, keeps the baseline, and reruns the audit
- --why is required; an existing path is required unless --new marks it as a file to create
- the new tier is printed; if the amendment raises the plan to standard or into a critical zone, the audit fails like any other plan missing those sections (exit 7), never silently waived
- audit.json is refreshed only on pass; on fail the plan is left amended and not standing
- each amendment is recorded in the plan (path, why, when) and in the event log; draft-pr and review-diff show the list, so a reviewer sees the plan widened after its audit
- plans without amendments validate exactly as before; schema bumped only if the file shape needs it
- the pre-tool-use hook's refusal message names wb sdd amend as the way through
- tests: happy path, missing --why, missing path without --new, tier raised to standard fails audit, amended plan claims its new file in scope.claims
